items.title: Item 1
items.text: Nike Streamlines China E-Commerce ------------------------------------ Nike (NYSE:NKE ) revealed plans late yesterday to overhaul its e-commerce distribution in China. Most online sales will be made through the company’s own website and app, and from Nike-branded storefronts on JD.com (NASDAQ:JD ), Tmall, and Douyin, while local store partners are expected to concentrate on physical retail. The stock was little changed in pre-market trading. * “These new flagships will serve as the single, elevated destination for Nike”: Cathy Sparks, vice president and general manager for Greater China, said the move “is about reducing fragmentation and strengthening the consumer journey,” adding, “When the experience is consistent, the brand becomes stronger.” * Greater China revenue fell 17% on a currency-neutral basis: The move is focused on returning the region to growth, and it comes after a year-over-year (YoY) revenue decline in the fourth quarter following a previous 10% drop in Q3. Discover how Nike's Q4 progress went Divider -----------------------------------

items.title: Item 2
items.text: Super Micro Pops as Orders Surge ----------------------------------- Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI ) popped more than 15% in pre-market trading after the AI server manufacturer said a rise in new orders in fiscal Q4 should see gross margins roughly double – from a prior guidance range of 8.2% to 8.4% up to a new range of 15% to 17%. * “Backlog rose to record levels at the end of fiscal 2026 with total new orders in excess of $60 billion received during the fourth quarter”: In a business update, Super Micro said the boost is “primarily due to a favorable customer and product mix.” * Dell and HPE ride Super Micro's coattails: Other companies in the server market enjoyed a knock-on effect. Dell (NYSE:DELL ) added over 4% this morning on top of yesterday’s 6% gain at close, with Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE ) adding a pre-market 3% in addition to yesterday’s 5% rise. items.text: How Much Should You Have Saved for Retirement? ------------------------------------------------- Robert Brokamp ROBERT BROKAMP, CFP, EA TEAM HIDDEN GEMS Figuring out whether you're on track to retire is a complicated calculation, involving many variables and a few predictions. What if you're just looking for a quick litmus test to see if you're generally on track? Well, you're in luck. Savings guidelines are regularly published and updated by a handful of financial services firms. Every few years, I publish an overview of these guidelines – updating the numbers with the latest research (and the numbers do often change). Let's take a look at the most recent retirement-savings benchmarks. Check if your nest egg is on track Divider -----------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 4
items.text: Pre-Market Q2 Results You Won’t Want to Miss ----------------------------------------------- * GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV ), recommended in Hidden Gems, beat Wall Street expectations with a 22% YoY revenue rise to reach $11.1 billion, 19% ahead of the $9.3 billion reported in Q1 . Management raised full-year guidance, and now expects revenue of $45.5 billion to $46.5 billion with free cash flow of $11.5 billion to $12.5 billion. Despite the upbeat results, the stock dipped 6% in early trading . * Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies (NYSE:WAB ) gained around 6% pre-market, after reporting 17.5% sales growth compared to the same quarter last year, reaching $3.18 billion – and beating expectations of around $3.07 billion . The increase was driven by both freight and transit divisions. WAB is recommended in SA by Team Hidden Gems. * CME Group (NASDAQ:CME ), a SA rec by Team Rule Breakers, reported $1.71 billion revenue in Q2, slightly ahead of expectations and up a little from $1.69 billion a year prior. CEO Terry Duffy told us “The first half of 2026 was the strongest in CME Group's history,” with record H1 performance across most headline measures. The stock edged up around 1% in response. See if CME matched Q2 expectations Divider ------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: Don’t Spend It All in One Place ------------------------------------------------ Jason Moser Younger companies are wise to reinvest cash flow back in the business. To do otherwise typically comes at the cost of growth and market share. Costco (NASDAQ:COST ) is an example of a company that reinvested heavily early in order to grow its store base and market share. Fast-forward to today and the long-term investors have won and the company dominates its space. — JASON MOSER • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to reveal the most important thing a company can do with its first few years of free cash flow – and which businesses have impressed you most with that decision – or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! items.title: Item 6
items.text: Your Take ------------ YESTERDAY’S TOP TAKE We asked, have you ever bought or sold a stock partly because a famous investor did? How did it work out, and what did you learn from following someone else's lead? J Member jbn said “I sold [Taiwan Semi (NYSE:TSM )] shares after learning that [Warren Buffett] shared my fear of putting too much trust in the stability of the China/Taiwan situation. While it's true that China wouldn't want to destroy the TSM chip/money machine, it's also true that Xi Jingping really wants to control Taiwan. I lost out on some gains, but I already had a significant gain on those shares and redeployed the money to other green and growing stocks. Did I lose out a bit, yes; did it lead to finding some other good investments, also yes.” See more great answers from our Foolish community in Breakfast News.
